title: Aramaic Root Atlas: A Cross-Corpus Triliteral Root Explorer
description:
The Aramaic Root Atlas is an open-access, cross-corpus triliteral root explorer for Aramaic literature. It indexes 5,666 roots across 47,358 verses and 685,848 words drawn from six corpora spanning roughly 1,500 years of literary history, bringing them under a single consonantal root index so a single Semitic root can be traced across textual traditions, scripts, and centuries.

Corpora indexed

  • Peshitta New Testament (Syriac)
  • Peshitta Old Testament (Syriac)
  • Biblical Aramaic — Daniel, Ezra, and related passages (Hebrew square script)
  • Targum Onkelos to the Torah (Hebrew square script)
  • Targum Jonathan to the Prophets (Hebrew square script)
  • Hymns of Ephrem of Nisibis — Carmina Nisibena (Syriac)

Cross-script normalization resolves Syriac and Hebrew square forms to a shared key (e.g. Syriac ܟܬܒ and Hebrew כתב both resolve to K-T-B), enabling unified search across scripts. The Atlas includes 1,655 cognate root entries with Hebrew and/or Arabic cognates and 405 Greek New Testament parallels.

Features: root-family visualization (force-directed graph + root card), KWIC concordance with TEI/CSV export, diachronic analysis, collocations, semantic-field classification (15 domains), morphological word parser, passage lexical profiles, a synoptic parallel viewer, root-frequency heat maps, researcher annotations and bookmarks, multi-format citation export (BibTeX, Chicago, MLA, APA, SBL), a guided tour, and an interactive Swagger/OpenAPI reference. The interface is quadrilingual (English, Spanish, Hebrew, Arabic) with full right-to-left support and a dark mode.

What's new in v3.1

  • New corpus — Targum Jonathan to the Prophets (Sefaria, CC-BY-SA): 9,296 verses and 157,449 words across 21 books (Joshua–II Kings, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and the Twelve), doubling Targumic coverage.
  • Unlocks synoptic comparison of the Peshitta Old Testament with Targum Jonathan for the Prophets in the parallel viewer.
  • Root index grows from 5,249 to 5,666 roots; cognate entries from 1,584 to 1,655 (newly attested Targum-Jonathan vocabulary enriched with Hebrew and Arabic cognates).
  • A distinct corpus color, full UI/i18n integration across all four languages, and Swagger coverage for the new corpus.
  • Numerous fixes surfaced during integration: cross-corpus book-name alignment (Samuel/Kings), root-card layout, diachronic label rendering, and corrected page titles and breadcrumbs.

How to cite

Fresco Benaim, Jose. (2026). Aramaic Root Atlas: A Cross-Corpus Triliteral Root Explorer (v3.1.0). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19358625

The concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19358625 always resolves to the latest version; cite a specific version DOI when reproducibility matters. A CITATION.cff with machine-readable metadata and BibTeX/Chicago/MLA/APA/SBL exports are available in-app and in the repository.
